co_master_s_wall.blurb: A small sport crag in Cunningham Gulch, a high valley above Silverton in the San Juans, reached by driving up the county road toward Howardsville. It holds around a dozen bolted lines, with one easy 5.8 at the left end, a cluster of 5.11s, a handful of 5.12s and a couple of 5.13s, so it suits stronger leaders far more than beginners. The rock is limestone. At roughly 11,000 feet it is a summer and early-fall destination, and the valley around it has waterfalls and good places to camp. Expect a quiet day with few other parties.

co_mezzanine.blurb: A small, tucked-away bouldering section within the Morrison boulders, west of Denver. You find it by walking along the base of the main wall past a horizontal pine, then continuing a short way up to a tiered ledge. About fourteen problems are listed, from a handful of easy sloping warm-ups through a solid middle of V3 to V5, topping out around V6, and a few lines may still be waiting to be cleaned. The sandstone is better than much of the nearby rock, and it sees fewer people than the busier Morrison walls.

co_dasani_area.blurb: Three boulders on the Dark Side hillside at Morrison, just off the main trail where the first problem appears on your right. From east to west they are the Warmup Boulder, the Dasani Boulder and the Cling Free Boulder, with the rock staircase leading up to the Cube close by. Fourteen problems spread from the easiest grades through a mid-range of V5 and V6 to a couple of much harder lines. The hillside is known for shade in summer, and the namesake Dasani problem is the most visited, making this a useful place to warm up and then try something harder. Rattlesnakes are reported in the area.

co_petrified_boulder.blurb: A single steep, north-leaning face in the Sailing Hawks boulders just outside Durango. Find it at the back of the main area: take the trail from the parking and continue uphill beyond the warm-up block. The sandstone is pebbly on the left and smoother to the right, and landings are generally good with problems tall enough to feel worthwhile without being scary. Fourteen lines cover everything from the easiest grades up to V9, with the middle grades around V2 to V6 well represented. The boulder is often suggested as a first warm-up, and it packs a lot of problems into one place.

co_main_boulder.blurb: The big, hard-to-miss block that anchors the Pink Floyd area of Nine Mile Hill, in Unaweep Canyon near Grand Junction. Its large face points east, and it is the first major stop on the trail in from the Mecca parking area. Fourteen problems range from a couple of V0s and a few mid-grade lines to a cluster around V5, then a few V7s and one very hard line near V10. The sandstone is vertical to slightly overhung, and the canyon wall behind shades the area earlier in the afternoon. It is a good place to warm up on easy lines before the harder test pieces.
